inventedEvidence.evidence: Hedged rather than stated as fact, but 'it is likely still under warranty' was asserted without ever asking the appliance's age (it is 4 years old, out of warranty).

rationale: The assistant correctly identified the door interlock/latch as the most likely cause, gave an appropriate high-voltage warning against opening the casing, suggested sensible safe checks (latch hooks/slots, button feel) and escalated to a Bosch engineer, which matches the ground truth. Weaknesses: it never asked the appliance's age yet told the customer it was 'likely still under warranty' (it is 4 years old, outside Bosch's 2-year cover), it slightly over-leaned on the customer's uncertain 'might sit lower' observation as supporting evidence, and it did not acknowledge the possibility of a control module fault or probe the closing-gently-vs-firmly pattern. Overall a UK homeowner would be reasonably well served but may be misled on warranty expectations.
